messages.author: bfa183f4897a5619
messages.subject: problems with spectro() and split.screen()
parts:
Hello,

When I try to print multiple spectrograms to a window using spectro() and split.screen(), I find that any previous spectrograms are erased when I draw a new one.

Example:

> data(tico)
> data(pellucens)
> close.screen(all=T)
> par(bg='white')
> split.screen(c(1,2))
[1] 1 2
> screen(1)
> spectro(tico, scale=F)
> screen(2)
> spectro(pellucens, scale=F)

The tico spectrogram disappears when I create the pellucens spectrogram.

Is there a way around this? I find that I can do multiple spectrograms in a window using par(mfrow) just fine, but I'd like to be able to have my spectrograms be of different sizes, as I would be able to do with split.screen().

I'm using the 64-bit R (version 1.14.0) on Windows 7.

Thanks very much!
Jesse Ross

messages.author: de80047cbc18c87e
messages.subject: Re: [seewave] problems with spectro() and split.screen()
parts:
Hello,

This seems to be due to the function filled.contour() called by spectro().

You can use layout() instead and play with the argument 'width':

> layout(matrix(1:2, nc=2), width=c(2,1))
> spectro(tico, scale=F)
> spectro(pellucens, scale=F)

HTH,

Jerome
